2026-11-11.meal: Air-fryer crispy gnocchi with roasted tomatoes, courgette & pesto
2026-11-11.note: Hockey Academy Night 6:15–7:45pm (The Lindum). Ready in 20 minutes either side of the run. (Swapped in because there's no Saturday curry in the freezer now.)

ingredients: Grated parmesan or vegetarian hard cheese, to serve
steps: Heat the air fryer to 200°C.
Toss the gnocchi, courgette and cherry tomatoes in the oil with a pinch of salt.
Air fry for 12–15 minutes, shaking the basket every 5 minutes, until the gnocchi is golden and crisp and the tomatoes have burst. (Do it in two batches if your basket is small.)
Tip into a big bowl and toss with the pesto, and the spinach if using.
Serve with cheese on top.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: give her some plain crispy gnocchi and tomatoes before the pesto goes in, with a little cheese.

2026-11-12.note: Mathilda's Scotter Primary open day this morning — evening's free, nothing on for tea

ingredients: Zest of 1 lemon, plus a squeeze of juice
Parmesan or vegetarian hard cheese, to serve
steps: Cook the pasta according to the pack instructions, then drain, saving a mugful of the water.
Season the salmon and pan-fry for 3–4 minutes each side until just cooked through, then flake into chunks.
In a separate pan, soften the leek in the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the peas and a splash of the pasta water, and cook for 2–3 minutes.
Stir in the crème fraîche and lemon zest, and warm through. Take out Mathilda's portion of sauce now if she's sensitive to lemon.
Add a squeeze of lemon juice to the rest, then toss the pasta through the sauce with the flaked salmon.
Serve with a sprinkle of cheese.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: flake her salmon extra small and check carefully for bones.

2026-11-13.note: Children in Need day at nursery, gymnastics & swimming done earlier — evening's free. Good day to batch-cook extra for tomorrow (busy with hockey, Franco's party and girls day).

steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder and cumin and cook for 1 minute.
Add the squash, chickpeas, chopped tomatoes and coconut milk. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook for 20-25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the squash is tender.
Take out Mathilda's portion and 4 portions to cool for Saturday before stirring the spinach into the remainder.
Cook for 3-4 minutes more until the spinach wilts.
Cook the rice and serve with the curry.
Cool the 4 extra portions within an hour, cover and keep in the fridge for Saturday (no need to freeze).
recipe.tip: Mathilda: keep hers mild and mash the squash a little finer if she's fussy about texture.

2026-11-14.meal: Reheat: Friday's butternut squash, chickpea & spinach curry
2026-11-14.note: Hockey open session this morning, girls day and Francis's party (3-5pm) today — quick reheat gets tea ready whenever everyone's trickled home.

steps: Tip the curry into a pan with a splash of water.
Heat gently, stirring, until bubbling and piping hot all the way through (about 8-10 minutes). Or microwave in a covered bowl for 4-5 minutes, stirring halfway.
Cook the rice while the curry heats.
Serve straightaway.
recipe.tip: Only reheat it once, and check it's piping hot all the way through before serving.

2026-11-15.note: This week's one meat night. Back from Francis's Wakefield hockey session by early afternoon — a good free evening to restock the freezer meal drawer, since both the frozen bolognese and curry have been used up recently. Alex away in Salisbury all week.

ingredients: 1 beef stock cube, dissolved in 200ml hot water
Parmesan or vegetarian hard cheese, to serve
steps: Soften the onions, garlic, carrots and celery in the oil in a large pan for 8 minutes.
Add the mince and brown for 8-10 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Stir in the tomatoes, purée, stock and herbs. Season, cover and simmer for 40-45 minutes, stirring now and then.
Take out Mathilda's portion, then cook the spaghetti for 10-12 minutes while the sauce finishes.
Serve tonight's portion over spaghetti with cheese.
Cool the rest completely within an hour (spreading it out in a shallow dish speeds this up), then portion into 6 containers, label with the contents and date, and freeze for the meal drawer.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: cut her spaghetti short and check the sauce isn't too chunky. Never freeze it while it's still warm — make sure it's fully cooled first.

2026-11-16.meal: Garlic butter baked haddock with crushed new potatoes & peas
2026-11-16.note: Mathilda's allergy appointment this morning, evening's free — nothing on for tea.

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Boil the new potatoes for 15-18 minutes until tender.
Mix the melted butter with the garlic and a squeeze of lemon. Put the haddock on a lined tray and brush over the butter.
Bake for 12-15 minutes, until the fish flakes easily.
Cook the peas for the last 4 minutes of the potatoes.
Drain and lightly crush the potatoes with a fork, stir through the parsley and a knob of butter.
Serve the fish with the crushed potatoes, peas and lemon wedges.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: leave the garlic butter off her portion and check carefully for bones.

2026-11-17.meal: Slow-cooker Mediterranean vegetable stew with butter beans & feta
2026-11-17.note: Hull hockey training 6-7pm (Hymers College) plus travel — slow cooker on by 9am so tea's ready for whoever's not driving, kept warm for the rest. Alex still away.

steps: Put the onion, garlic, courgette, aubergine and peppers into the slow cooker.
Add the butter beans, chopped tomatoes, tomato purée and oregano. Stir well and season.
Cover and cook on low for 6-7 hours (or high for 3-4), until the veg is tender.
Take out Mathilda's portion and set aside before crumbling the feta over the rest.
Serve with crusty bread.
recipe.tip: On by 9am before the school run. Mathilda: keep hers plain without the feta, and mash a few of the veg chunks if she's fussy about texture.

2026-11-18.meal: Air-fryer peri-peri cod with sweet potato wedges & corn
2026-11-18.note: Dentist appointment for all three of you 4-5pm, then straight into Hockey Academy Night 6:15-7:45pm — air fryer gets tea done fast in the gap between.

ingredients: 1-2 tsp peri-peri seasoning (to taste, for the grown-ups' portions)
steps: Heat the air fryer to 200°C. Toss the sweet potato wedges in half the oil and a pinch of salt, and air fry for 12 minutes.
Meanwhile rub the cod with the rest of the oil. Keep 1-2 fillets completely plain for the kids, and rub peri-peri seasoning onto the grown-ups' fillets only.
Add the cod to the air fryer basket alongside the wedges and cook for a further 8-10 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily and the wedges are crisp.
Heat the sweetcorn in a small pan or the microwave for 3-4 minutes.
Serve the cod and wedges with the sweetcorn.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: keep her cod and wedges completely plain, no peri-peri. Ready in 20 minutes either side of the dentist/hockey run.

2026-11-19.meal: Fish pie with mashed potato topping
2026-11-19.note: Free evening, nothing on for tea — a cosy one to round off the week.

ingredients: 600g mixed fish (e.g. salmon, smoked haddock & raw king prawns), cut into chunks
25g butter, plus extra for the mash
1 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped (or 1 tsp dried)
steps: Boil the potatoes for 15-18 minutes until tender, then drain and mash with butter and a splash of milk.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Melt the 25g butter in a pan, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the milk. Simmer for 3-4 minutes, stirring, until thickened.
Stir the fish, peas and parsley into the sauce. Take out Mathilda's portion into a small ovenproof dish now.
Pour the rest into a large ovenproof dish, top with the mash, and scatter over the cheese if using.
Bake for 25-30 minutes (20 minutes for Mathilda's smaller dish), until golden on top and piping hot all the way through — check the fish is cooked and opaque before serving.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: check carefully for bones and let her portion cool a little before serving, as it comes out hotter than it looks.
